clue.text: Bores doctor with ailments

parts.note: ailments are ills, minor sicknesses

explanation.surface: A tedious doctor drones on about his patients' complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to drill it, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow taken in by loaded dice? It's resulting in losses

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the rearranged letters
loaded dice are weighted to fall differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A gambler's crooked dice end up costing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' makes DEIC from the dice, and 'taken in by' puts the fellow inside. 'resulting in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall, an amount lost or lacking.

clue.text: Merit in being treated, having temporary effect

indicators.note: being treated means being processed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical remark that a treatment works only for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim measure is provisional, in force only until something permanent replaces it.

clue.text: At Our Lady's, Barking, offering praise

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: At a church named for Our Lady, in Barking in east London, a hymn of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here 'barking' is British slang for mad, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory language expresses praise or commendation.

clue.text: Attach legal condition to place for storing wine and port

parts.note: a wine bin is a rack or store for bottles
Dover is the English Channel ferry port in Kent

explanation.surface: A cellar description that somehow drifts into legal language.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is a ferry port on England's south coast. In British law a magistrate can bind someone over, placing them under a legal obligation to keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding someone over in court imposes a condition on their future conduct, under threat of a penalty.

clue.text: Such behaviour, say, I consider is odd

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that they find a habit strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such behaviour' means the odd behaviour the rest of the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiosyncrasies are peculiar personal habits, odd ways of acting.

clue.text: Condescend to plan without having succeeded

indicators.note: without means leaving out the letter

parts.note: a design is a plan
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to make a plan that never quite worked.
explanation.walkthrough: S for 'succeeded' comes from family trees and lists of monarchs. 'having' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something one considers beneath oneself.

clue.text: Vital contents of trunk?

parts.note: the trunk is the human torso, not a box for luggage, and its vital contents are the internal organs

explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body cavity.

clue.text: Note journalists like an organ

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
ED, short for editor, stands for journalists
ED, short for editor, stands for journalists

explanation.surface: A remark that reporters resemble a body part, or an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'journalists', gives ED twice, as two editors. An organ has reeds in its pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reeded is fitted with reeds, as some pipes of the instrument are.

clue.text: Part of modern appliance chips are put in

definitions.text: Part of modern appliance chips are put in

parts.words: Part of modern appliance chips are put in
parts.note: it reads like a fridge or oven that frozen chips go into, but the chips are silicon ones, the processing component inside smart devices

explanation.definitionFit: A computer's processing unit on silicon chips sits inside today's household gadgets.

clue.text: Pasta — is it cut fine when cooked?

indicators.note: cooking changes the state of the ingredients, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether the pasta ribbons get sliced thin during preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges IT CUT FINE; 'is' only links the definition to the wordplay. This spelling of the ribbon pasta is a variant of the commoner one ending -INE.
explanation.definitionFit: These flat ribbon noodles are a familiar Italian variety of the food named.

clue.text: Children's edition

definitions.meaning: offspring, in the legal phrase 'died without'
one printing of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's lineal descendants in legal language, and a periodical's number is a release of it.

clue.text: French horns introducing tune for ballet hero

parts.note: cor is French for horn, so the plural is cors
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: The horn section plays the theme that announces the dancer in the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' just says the horns come before the tune. 'French horns' looks like the brass instrument but means horns in French. Le Corsaire is a ballet whose hero is a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of the ballet Le Corsaire is a pirate, a privateer of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Open wrong brand, say

parts.note: a wrong is a sin, an offence

indicators.note: say signals that the word for brand is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to brand with a hot iron is to sear

explanation.surface: Someone opens a mislabelled product, or so they claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you that only the sound of SEAR is wanted; it is written CERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open is frank and honest, without pretence.

clue.text: Pace a short time, then mope about

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of mope are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone paces for a little while, then sulks around the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MOPE to EMPO. 'a' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or speed of movement, especially in music.

clue.text: Timely wordplay — cut out a line

parts.note: a pun is play on words

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of cut are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a writer: drop the joke and cut a line so the piece is on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on time and being prompt mean the same thing.

clue.text: Check suitability of coordinates for sporting event

parts.note: to test something is to check whether it is suitable
to match items is to coordinate them

explanation.surface: Someone checks a colour scheme before a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket or rugby fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a full international fixture, especially in cricket.

clue.text: Without losses, having suffered no strikes?

definitions.meaning: never defeated in a run of games

explanation.definitionFit: An undefeated side has lost no games, and someone never struck has not been hit.

clue.text: One desirous of good company, presumably

definitions.text: One desirous of good company, presumably

parts.words: One desirous of good company, presumably
parts.note: company here means a troupe of actors, so this is a theatre-goer hoping for a fine cast rather than a sociable person

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre-goer wants to watch a strong troupe of actors perform.

clue.text: Kind of stage lighting

definitions.meaning: a level platform at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: A stair platform is one sense, and coming to rest after flight, as a bird alights, is the other.

clue.text: Son still in prime

parts.note: even means still, as in 'even better'

explanation.surface: A boy is still in the best years of his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime' looks like 'in his prime' but is the noun for a number divisible only by itself and one.
explanation.definitionFit: The number named is divisible only by itself and one, a prime number.

clue.text: Flowers? Maybe it's love!

indicators.note: maybe suggests another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A gift of a bouquet is perhaps a sign of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: These small purple blooms are a species of spring plant.

clue.text: Start to decorate interior for feast

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the interior is the inner part

explanation.surface: A host starts decorating the inside of the house for a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner, especially a formal one, is a substantial meal or feast.

clue.text: Base in which I belong, getting new order

indicators.note: the letters given a new order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a foundation where they fit in, rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the moral sense is dishonourable, lacking nobility.

clue.text: Glorify Lady in the Lake? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: in, taken with what follows, describes one piece placed inside another
this swaps the roles, so the lake goes inside the lady instead

parts.note: Bess is a woman's name, short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Should one praise the legendary Lady of the Lake, or the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady of the Lake is a figure from Arthurian legend; 'Quite the reverse' means put the lake (L) in the lady (BESS).
explanation.definitionFit: To bless God is to praise or glorify him.

clue.text: Total gained, say, for important person

indicators.note: say tells us the words sum and won are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sum is a total; won means gained

explanation.surface: Someone tots up their earnings to impress a VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being somebody, a person of note, is to be important.

clue.text: One's taken in by Welshman turning green

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the other piece
turning signals the name is read backwards

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a Welshman who is turning pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EVAN to NAVE, and 'taken in by' puts I inside it. 'green' looks like a colour but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or gullible.

clue.text: Short, short time in steam's cooked confection

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the rearranged letters
cooked means altered, so the letters of steam are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
wee is Scottish for small
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: steam it briefly to make a sugary treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes SMEAT; 'in' slips the two short pieces in after its S. Wee is Scottish for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is a sugary delicacy, a candied confection.

clue.text: Repository of records about essential limits of remedy

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the essential of something is its gist

indicators.note: limits of means the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An archive holding notes on the core features of a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A registry is an office where official records are kept.

clue.text: Chapter one's rewritten, as decided

indicators.note: rewritten means put down in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author rewrites a chapter after making up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges ONES to OSEN. 'as' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chosen has been picked or selected, settled on.
